components.k: Global macro (dollar, yields, EM flows, rupee, oil)
India growth & earnings (GDP, inflation, earnings, profitability)

checks.why: Faster real growth usually supports company sales and profits.

checks.k: Growth direction (next year vs this year)
checks.why: Accelerating growth is a tailwind; a slowdown is a headwind.
Inflation inside the central bank's 2–6% band keeps interest rates and costs in check.
Over long periods company earnings tend to grow roughly in line with nominal GDP.
Trailing earnings per index unit, from the index level and its P/E.

checks.k: Nifty 50 earnings growth (3 years, a year)
checks.why: Earnings keeping pace with the economy is a sign of healthy profits.
Model earnings growth = next year's nominal GDP forecast; a lower P/E per point of growth is more attractive.

checks.k: Profitability of Nifty 50 companies (return on equity)
checks.why: Fund-house analysts watch return on equity: 15%+ shows companies earn well on shareholders' money; below 12% is weak.

checks.k: Earnings breadth (sector indices with rising earnings)
checks.why: Broad-based profit growth across sectors is healthier than gains led by a few sectors.
The 500 largest listed companies, about 90% of the market's value, show the trend beyond the top 50.
